Resolves #20095

A revealed item's toolbar is now its header. It carries the item's pop-out, gated exactly as the docked header gates it. Using it pops the railed item out through the docked pop-out's own admission path, measured at the reveal's pane. The item detaches still `autoHidden`, so closing its window returns it to its rail. An app-held reveal pops out through the same entry (`Workspace#popOutRailItem`). Every reveal end now names its cause on `dockRailRevealChange`, so an application holding a reveal can tell a person's dismissal from the item leaving its rail.

The reveal's pop-out is the docked pop-out's own transaction (`HeaderActions#popOutDockItem`: measure, admit, hand off, detach, witness), entered from the reveal. Only the hand-off is new: a rail destroys a cached, config-built reveal pane when its item leaves, and by then that pane is inside the vessel. So the rail yields it, alive, before the detach (`Rail#yieldRevealPane`), and the tear-out holds it as the handle adoption moves (`TearOut#capturePane(itemId, pane)`). A workspace that declined the HeaderActions plugin binds no reveal pop-out.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — five lines: the public seam an app-held reveal pops out through (AC-3), a one-line delegate like `recreateDockPane`, and its two projection wires; the transaction lives in the HeaderActions plugin

Evidence: L2 (component and unit specs in headless Chromium) → L2 required (AC-1 through AC-5). The real-window leg is the drag tear-out's e2e (`DemoBDockTearOutNL`), which this click enters through the same pair. Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket
- **AC-2 narrowed in the body before this PR.** The reveal's pin restores a railed item, the inverse of the docked header's pin, so it keeps its own `restorable` policy. Maximize is a node's action, which a railed item has no node for. The authority is Clio's design read on Institution #791 (Q1 (a): "pin, pop-out, maximize where the item has them").
- **Cause vocabulary.** The ticket named the person, the application and the item. A retarget also ends the item it leaves, so a tab click, a hover dwell and an application `hold` onto another item carry `tab`, `hover` and `hold`.
- **No deletion in the engine.** The consumer lines this lets go are in the Institution follow-up: `pinRevealedDetail` and its six journeys' calls, plus the cockpit's own dismissal flag, which reads `cause` instead.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:**
- **Answering your question on `Workspace.mjs:2584` (`dockRailPopOutBinding: me.getPlugin?.('dock-header-actions') && (railId => me.dockHeaderActionPolicy?.createRailPopOutBinding(railId))`) + post-projection plugin attachment nuance (non-blocking):**
  Yes — gating `dockRailPopOutBinding` in `Workspace`'s projection options (`Workspace.mjs:2584`) is the right boundary. `HeaderActionPolicy` (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs:169–175`) owns pure state-provider formula truth (`!!this.getData('dock.rails.<railId>.revealed') && this.getData('dock.popOutAvailable') === true && this.getData('dockActionPolicy.pop-out') !== false`), whereas `Workspace` is the composition root that knows whether `enableDockHeaderActionsPlugin: false` declined the executor (`HeaderActions`). Putting the plugin check inside `HeaderActionPolicy` would couple a pure state-binding factory to plugin lookup on the host component.
  *One subtle edge case to keep in mind (non-blocking):* because `me.getPlugin?.('dock-header-actions')` is evaluated when `projectDockModel()` builds the `LayoutAdapter` options (`Workspace.mjs:2584`), it relies on `enableDockHeaderActionsPlugin` being a construction-time config (`Workspace#construct` creates the `HeaderActions` plugin before `projectDockModel()` runs). If a future caller ever attached `HeaderActions` dynamically *after* the initial `projectDockModel()` pass without re-projecting, the existing `Rail` instances would not have `bind.dockRevealPopOut` wired until the next projection. Since `enableDockHeaderActionsPlugin` is strictly construction-time in `Workspace`, the current gate is exact.
- **Refused detach commit after `itemCleared` (`HeaderActions.mjs:246–257`, non-blocking observation):**
  In `HeaderActions#popOutRailItem`, `handOff()` runs *after* `admitDockPopOut` succeeds (`HeaderActions.mjs:295–304`) and calls `rail.yieldRevealPane(itemId)`, `me.tearOutHandlers.capturePane(itemId, yielded.pane)`, and `rail.revealMachine.itemCleared(itemId)` before `onDockTearOutTerminal`. If the host's `admitDockPopOut` declines the vessel (the normal refusal path tested in `DockPopOut.spec.mjs:298–313`), `handOff()` never runs and the reveal stays open untouched. If `admitDockPopOut` *admits* the vessel (`true`) but the subsequent `onDockTearOutTerminal` detach commit is refused by the reducer (`detached === false`), `restore()` releases the captured pane from `tearOutHandlers` and restores `rail.revealPaneCache[itemId] = yielded.pane`, while the reveal overlay remains closed (`idle`). That is a clean fail-safe state (cached pane preserved for the next reveal, no leaked `capturedPanes` entry).
